## Setup and rationale

Load the package and get the data.

```{r}
library(whereipm)
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)

# loading the data
data <- ipmdata

# subsetting for pools and females only
data <- data %>%
  filter(sex == "F" & habitat == "P")

# defining colours to be used
Cols <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Zissou1", 6, type = "continuous")[6:1]
```

Instead of running three separate models using three distinct phases, we can run a single model specifying time as a covariate.

This can by considering time a continuous variable (either as year or month), and then picking three representative time points to depict the phases.

What this approach allows to do is to capture a larger sample of, i.e. local densities, which can illuminate on behaviours of vital rates only observable at extreme (e.g. very high) density values. This can be especially true for survival or reproduction, which can show a quadratic relationship with local density (initial Allee affect, followed by density regulation).

Here, I will define a variable (`year`) that I might use later to subset the results.

```{r}
# defining alternative variables
# Year
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    year = cut(sampling, 
               breaks = c(0, 13, 25, 37, 49, 62),
               labels = 1:5) %>% as.factor
  )
```

## Models

I can now run separate models using different time specifications, and check the model fit.
As I did for the phase models in [a previous vignette](vignette(DIPM-020_Vital_rate_models)), I will run separate models for:

1. Survival;
2. Recruitment;
3. Adult dispersal probability;
4. Adult dispersal distance;
5. Natal dispersal probability;
6. Natal dispersal distance.

### 1. Survival

Survival could show a quadratic relationwhip with local density. This could be due to Allee effects causing survival to increase with density up to a given threshold, followed by survival depression by competition over resources, at higher local densities.

Here, I will run models, (a linear model and two quardatic models) and compare the fit through AIC.

```{r, results = "asis"}
# Here I will test which of the models containing or not a quadratic term for density fits best
# linear model
survTimeL <- lme4::glmer(survival ~ s_time*s_loc_density
                            + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (s_loc_density|sampling),
                          data=data,
                          family=binomial,
                          lme4::glmerControl(optimizer=c('bobyqa')),
                          na.action = na.omit)
# quadratic model
survTimeQI <- lme4::glmer(survival ~ s_time*(s_loc_density + I(s_loc_density^2))
                            + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (s_loc_density|sampling),
                          data=data,
                          family=binomial,
                          lme4::glmerControl(optimizer=c('bobyqa')),
                          na.action = na.omit)

# quadratic model without quadratic interaction
survTimeQ <- lme4::glmer(survival ~ s_time*(s_loc_density) + I(s_loc_density^2)
                            + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (s_loc_density|sampling),
                          data=data,
                          family=binomial,
                          lme4::glmerControl(optimizer=c('bobyqa')),
                          na.action = na.omit)

anova(survTimeL, survTimeQ, survTimeQI)
# both quadratic models have much better fit than the linear model, so I will keep the most simple of them, for parsimony
surv <- survTimeQ

stargazer::stargazer(survTimeL, survTimeQI, survTimeQ,
                     type = "html",
                     column.labels = c("linear", "quadratic + i","quadratic"),
                     dep.var.labels = c("Survival"),
                     report = "vcp*",
                     column.sep.width = "10pt")
```


Drawing some plots to understand how survival changes with time.

```{r}
# making up some values for time and density
t <- 12*(0:5)/scalingAttr$time$scale
d <- seq(0, 100, by =1)/scalingAttr$loc_density$scale

# extracting fixed effects
fixef <- as.numeric(summary(survTimeQ)$coefficients[,"Estimate"])

# creating data matrix
toplot <- expand.grid(density = d, time = t)
# creating model matrix
mm <- model.matrix(object = ~ time*(density) + I(density^2), data = toplot)

toplot$predicted <- plogis(mm%*%fixef)

plot(0, col = "white", xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,1), las = 1, 
     ylab = "survival probability", xlab = "density (n/m)", main = "quadratic model (w/out interaction)")
for(i in unique(toplot$time)){
  lines(predicted~I(density*scalingAttr$loc_density$scale),
        data = toplot[toplot$time==i,],
        col = Cols[round(i*3)+1])
}
legend("bottomleft", lty = 1, legend = 12*0:5, col = Cols, title = "months")
```



### 2. Recruitment

As with Survival, reproduction could have a quadratic relationship with density. It is likely very low local density will cause low chances of reproducing, whereas high local density can decrease the number of offspring that survives to recruitment.

```{r}
# linear model
recrTimeL <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(recruited ~ s_time*s_loc_density +
                                + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (1|sampling),
                              ziformula = ~ s_time*s_loc_density +
                                + (1|FishID) +  (1|reach) + (1|sampling),
                              family="truncated_poisson"(link="log"),
                              data = data,
                              na.action = na.omit)

# quadratic model
recrTimeQI <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(recruited ~ s_time*(s_loc_density + I(s_loc_density^2)) +
                                + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (1|sampling),
                              ziformula = ~ s_time*(s_loc_density + I(s_loc_density^2)) +
                                + (1|FishID) +  (1|reach) + (1|sampling),
                              family="truncated_poisson"(link="log"),
                              data = data,
                              na.action = na.omit)

# quadratic model without quadratic interaction
recrTimeQ <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(recruited ~ s_time*s_loc_density + I(s_loc_density^2) +
                                + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (1|sampling),
                              ziformula = ~ s_time*s_loc_density + I(s_loc_density^2) +
                                + (1|FishID) +  (1|reach) + (1|sampling),
                              family="truncated_poisson"(link="log"),
                              data = data,
                              na.action = na.omit)

AIC(recrTimeL, recrTimeQ, recrTimeQI)
anova(recrTimeQI, recrTimeQ, recrTimeL)
# The linear models as a marginally better fit than the quadratic model with interaction.
# I will keep the linear for parsimony
recr <- recrTimeL

sjPlot::tab_model(recrTimeL, recrTimeQI, recrTimeQ,
                  show.icc = F, show.aic = T, show.se = T, show.est = T,
                  dv.labels = c("linear", "quadratic + i", "quadratic"),
                  show.ci = F)
```

```{r}
# plotting recruitment
toplot <- expand.grid(density = d, time = t)
fixef_zi <- as.numeric(summary(recrTimeL)$coefficients$zi[,"Estimate"])
fixef_cond <- as.numeric(summary(recrTimeL)$coefficients$cond[,"Estimate"])
mm <- model.matrix(object = ~ time*density, data = toplot)
toplot$predicted_zi <- 1 - plogis(mm%*%fixef_zi)
toplot$predicted_cond <- untruncZTP(mm%*%fixef_cond)

# reproduction probability plot
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(0, col = "white", xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,1), las = 1, 
     ylab = "reproduction probability", xlab = "density (n/m)")
for(i in unique(toplot$time)){
  lines(predicted_zi~I(density*scalingAttr$loc_density$scale),
        data = toplot[toplot$time==i,],
        col = Cols[round(i*3)+1])
}
legend("topright", lty = 1, legend = 12*0:5, col = Cols, title = "month")
# offspring number plot
plot(0, col = "white", xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(1,2.5), las = 1, 
     ylab = "n of recruits", xlab = "density (n/m)")
for(i in unique(toplot$time)){
  lines(predicted_cond~I(density*scalingAttr$loc_density$scale),
        data = toplot[toplot$time==i,],
        col = Cols[round(i*3)+1])
}
legend("topright", lty = 1, legend = 12*0:5, col = Cols, title = "month")
mtext("linear model", side = 3, outer = T)
```


### 3-4. Adult dispersal

For dispersal, I will use the models selected in the DDD MS (please see [DD-dispersal](https://gitlab.com/sebadebona/DD-dispersal)).

```{r}
# Dispersal probability
adDispP <- lme4::glmer(p_moving ~ s_time*s_loc_density  +
                               + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (s_loc_density|sampling),
                             family = 'binomial',
                             data = data,
                             lme4::glmerControl(optimizer=c('bobyqa')))

# Dispersal distance
adDispD <- lme4::lmer(log(dist_moved) ~ s_time +
                                 + (1|FishID) + (1|reach) + (1|sampling),
                               data = data)
# local density doesn't affect distance dispersed, but I will keep time to account for changes
```

```{r}
# plotting the results
toplot <- expand.grid(density = d, time = t)
fixef_p <- as.numeric(summary(adDispP)$coefficients[,"Estimate"])
mm_p <- model.matrix(object = ~ time*density, data = toplot)
toplot$predicted_p <- plogis(mm_p%*%fixef_p)

fixef_d <- as.numeric(summary(adDispD)$coefficients[,"Estimate"])
mm_d <- model.matrix(object = ~ time, data = toplot)
toplot$predicted_d <- exp(mm_d%*%fixef_d)

par(mfrow = c(1,2))
# dispersal probabilty plot
plot(0, col = "white", xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,1), las = 1, 
     ylab = "dispersal probability", xlab = "density (n/m)", "linear model")
for(i in unique(toplot$time)){
  lines(predicted_p~I(density*scalingAttr$loc_density$scale),
        data = toplot[toplot$time==i,],
        col = Cols[round(i*3)+1])
}
# dispersal distance plot
plot(0, col = "white", xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,15), las = 1, 
     ylab = "distance (m)", xlab = "density (n/m)", main = "time effect only")
for(i in unique(toplot$time)){
  lines(predicted_d~I(density*scalingAttr$loc_density$scale),
        data = toplot[toplot$time==i,],
        col = Cols[round(i*3)+1])
}
legend("topright", lty = 1, legend = 12*0:5, col = Cols, title = "month")
```


### 5-6. Natal dispersal

```{r}
# Natal dispersal probability
natDispP <- lme4::glmer(p_natal ~ s_time.birth + s_loc_density.mid*s_land_density.mid +
                           + (1|Maternity) + (1|reach.birth) + (s_loc_density.mid|sampling.birth),
                         family = 'binomial',
                         data = subset(data, mummoved == 0),
                         lme4::glmerControl(optimizer=c('bobyqa')))
summary(natDispP)

natDispD <- lme4::lmer(log(dist_natal) ~ s_time.birth + 
                     + (1|Maternity) + (1|reach.birth) 
                     + (1|sampling.birth),
                     data = subset(data, mummoved == 0))
summary(natDispD)
car::Anova(natDispD, type = "III")
```
```{r}
# plotting
toplot <- expand.grid(density = d, time = t, landscape = seq(0,12, by = 4)/scalingAttr$land_density$scale)
fixef_p <- as.numeric(summary(natDispP)$coefficients[,"Estimate"])
mm_p <- model.matrix(object = ~ time + density*landscape, data = toplot)
toplot$predicted_p <- plogis(mm_p%*%fixef_p)

par(mfrow = c(2,2))
for(j in unique(toplot$landscape)){
  plot(0, col = "white", xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,1), las = 1, 
     ylab = "dispersal probability", xlab = "density (n/m)", "linear model")
for(i in unique(toplot$time)){
  lines(predicted_p~I(density*scalingAttr$loc_density$scale),
        data = toplot[toplot$time==i & toplot$landscape==j,],
        col = Cols[round(i*3)+1])
  text(paste("landscape density =", round(j*scalingAttr$land_density$scale), sep=" "), x = 0, y = 0.1, pos = 4)
}}

legend("topright", lty = 1, legend = seq(0,10, by = 2), col = Cols, title = "landscape \ndensity")

# dispersal distance plot
toplot <- expand.grid(density = d, time = t)
fixef_d <- as.numeric(summary(natDispD)$coefficients[,"Estimate"])
mm_d <- model.matrix(object = ~ time, data = toplot)
toplot$predicted_d <- exp(mm_d%*%fixef_d)

plot(0, col = "white", xlim = c(0,100), ylim = c(0,30), las = 1, 
     ylab = "distance (m)", xlab = "density (n/m)", main = "time effect only")
for(i in unique(toplot$time)){
  lines(predicted_d~I(density*scalingAttr$loc_density$scale),
        data = toplot[toplot$time==i,],
        col = Cols[round(i*3)+1])
}
legend("topright", lty = 1, legend = 12*0:5, col = Cols, title = "month")
```

## Saving models

Here I am storing away the models for future use (building the IPMs)

```{r}
# only the selected models are stored away
singleVRModels <- tibble(survival = list(surv),
                         recruitment = list(recr),
                         adDispersal = list(adDispP),
                         adDistance = list(adDispD),
                         natDispersal = list(natDispP),
                         natDistance = list(natDispD))
saveRDS(singleVRModels, file = file.path(here::here(), "results", "singleVRModels.rds"))
```
